identity: The machine works of District 8: the soot-choked cupola tenders, scarred molders, and stokers who bleed to keep the coast in iron. The great furnace is fired only when the frost-heaved ice road can bear the weight of coal caravans. It speaks in a grueling schedule rather than a whistle—a rhythm of roaring heat and exhausted collapse. Without their castings, the Cut loses its deep anchors, the membrane hall's pipes rupture, and Block C slowly starves behind salvaged tin. They are exact, fiercely proud, and internally fracturing—pitting quotas against crushed limbs, and the insatiable hunger of the Cluster against their own survival.

relationships.notes: Brine pipe and valve bodies for iodine and grade salt; the Office audits every heat against its schedule (the Brine Pipe Exchange).
Coal and wreck scrap hauled south across the Cut at column rates; ice anchors and cleats owed in quotas (the Road Iron Charter, the Cluster Labour Schedule).
Winch drums and runners for the barge and Berth 9; the Fleet's levy on deep-coast salvage keeps the yard honest.
The Archivists log heats, incidents, and accord cycles; a works is only as good as its record.
Plowshares and heavy tools move through the exchange for seed and stores.
The Barons sell a place in the queue; the foundry casts valve bodies that outlast their contracts.
The foundry buys wreck scrap only with a clean claim mark — the crashed convoy and the dredger hulk have debts of their own.
No code, no contract, no questions. The foundry will not melt iron taken off a contested hull.
